instruction: Design the main gameplay screen (a single page) for a fast downhill Sliding Challenge game. Include a dramatic icy slope as the focal play field, a rider in motion, a clearly readable route, gates and obstacles ahead, speed and distance HUD, directional controls, and a compact progress indicator. Put strong emphasis on the sensation of speed, immediate obstacle readability, a distinct alpine identity, clear hierarchy, and polished visual finish.

history.critique: The artifact fails catastrophically on Brief & Intent Alignment because the central play field is entirely empty; the 'dramatic icy slope,' 'rider in motion,' 'route,' 'gates,' and 'obstacles' are completely missing, leaving only a dark void. This creates a severe Clarity & Information Hierarchy failure where the HUD elements (speed, time, progress) float in a vacuum with no visual context or focal point, making the 'gameplay' impossible to perceive. While the Visual System & Craft of the isolated UI components is high-quality—featuring clean typography, a consistent dark palette, and precise spacing—the overall composition is broken due to the lack of a scene. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness is also weak because the 'alpine identity' is limited to a single text label ('Königsberg Run') and a generic blue/orange color scheme, lacking any environmental texture, lighting, or atmospheric depth that would convey the sensation of a fast downhill slide.
history.suggestion: 1. **Implement the Core Scene (Critical):** Immediately populate the central void with a CSS-based 3D perspective slope. Use a large, angled `div` with a linear gradient (white to light blue) to simulate ice, adding a repeating linear gradient for texture. 2. **Add Rider & Motion:** Create a simple CSS shape for the rider positioned at the bottom center. Apply a `transform: translateZ()` or scale animation to simulate forward motion. Add 'speed lines' (thin, semi-transparent white divs) that move rapidly upward to create the sensation of speed. 3. **Integrate Route & Obstacles:** Draw a dashed white line down the center of the slope to represent the route. Place distinct, high-contrast geometric shapes (e.g., red/white striped divs) along the path to serve as gates and obstacles, ensuring they are clearly readable against the ice. 4. **Enhance Alpine Atmosphere:** Add a subtle vignette or fog effect at the top of the screen to create depth. Introduce a dynamic lighting effect (a radial gradient following the rider) to enhance the 'icy' feel and improve the visual hierarchy by drawing the eye to the action.

Trade-offs: The designer clearly invested in HUD polish (craft) at the expense of the actual scene (brief). The resolution must prioritize building the scene while keeping the good HUD system. Prioritized revision plan:
1. Build the focal scene first: a perspective icy slope filling the center, drawn with CSS gradients / SVG / canvas — a vanishing-point road/track with ice sheen, snow banks, distant peaks. This is the #1 fix.
2. Add the rider in motion at the lower-center of the slope, with motion streaks / speed lines / particle spray to convey velocity.
3. Lay out a readable route: a centerline / edge rails, with gates (pairs of poles) and obstacles (ice chunks, rocks) placed along the perspective, scaling with depth, color-coded for instant readability (gates = bright cyan/white, hazards = warm/red or dark rock).
4. Re-hierarchy the HUD: make the scene the focal point; demote the speed readout to a corner or keep bottom-center but smaller; consolidate the redundant steer controls (keep the dial OR the arrows, not both — or make arrows the primary and dial a visual indicator). Move timer/score to a single top-left cluster, progress to top-right, speed to bottom — ensure clear zones.
5. Inject alpine identity: cold palette (ice blue, snow white, deep sky), snow particles, frost vignette, mountain silhouette; keep orange as the "heat/boost" accent for contrast.
6. Speed sensation: tie visual effects to the speed value (streak intensity, FOV, particle rate), animate the slope scrolling.
7. Polish: ensure no clipping, consistent type scale, the progress segmented bar should clearly show 7/18 with the current gate highlighted.

history.critique: BRIEF & INTENT: The single most severe failure is that the focal play field is entirely absent — the center ~70% of the canvas is a flat empty navy void. There is no icy slope, no rider in motion, no route, no gates, and no obstacles, so the core 'fast downhill sliding' experience is not delivered at all; what exists is only a HUD floating over nothing. The required speed/distance HUD, steer control, boost gauge, and progress indicator ARE present and legible, but polish on the chrome cannot excuse the omission of the world. CLARITY & HIERARCHY: Priority is inverted — the blank center should be the hero but carries zero information, while four HUD clusters (top-left stats, top-center LIVE pill, top-right progress, bottom speed/steer/boost) compete for attention with no clear focal anchor. There is also a direct data contradiction: top-left shows 'x4.0 LINE COMBO' while bottom-center shows 'x1.0' with no label distinguishing them, so the player cannot tell which multiplier is active or what either means. The bottom edge is overcrowded (steer dial + 3 buttons + speed panel + boost ring all colliding in one band). VISUAL SYSTEM & CRAFT: The HUD components themselves are competent and consistent (rounded panels, monospace numerals, a tasteful cyan→orange speed gradient, a clean boost ring), but the system has no world to frame, so it reads as a settings/dashboard screen rather than a game. The steer knob is a generic glowing circle with no alpine or vehicle character. The palette is near-monochrome dark navy + orange, which is precise but flat and offers no depth, lighting, or material. EXPRESSIVENESS & DISTINCTIVENESS: There is no sense of speed (no motion streaks, parallax, blur, snow spray, or camera lean), no memorable moment, and almost no alpine identity beyond the word 'KÖNIGSBERG' — no snow, ice, sky, or mountain. The artifact is a generic dark dashboard, not a distinct alpine downhill game.
history.suggestion: Treat the empty play field as priority #1 and rebuild the screen around it, then re-tune the HUD to frame it. (1) FOCAL SLOPE: Fill the center with a perspective icy slope using only self-contained CSS/SVG — a cold sky gradient at top fading to snow-white, distant mountain silhouettes, a converging vanishing point, layered ice-sheen gradients and faint carved-track lines, plus a vignette for depth. (2) RIDER + SPEED SENSE: Place a CSS/SVG rider mid-slope in a lean, with animated speed lines, a motion-blur trail, and looping snow-spray particles so velocity is felt, not just read. (3) READABLE ROUTE: Draw the route as a center track with gates (paired poles + flags) and obstacles (ice blocks/rocks) receding in perspective; make the NEXT gate the largest and brightest, color-code gates (ice-cyan/white) vs obstacles (amber/red) for instant readability, and add a small 'next gate' direction arrow. (4) HIERARCHY FIX: Shrink and reposition HUD so the slope+rider+next-gate form the visual focal chain; keep speed as the largest number but anchor it as a single bottom 'dashboard' strip; move the steer dial to a clear corner so it no longer collides with the speed panel and boost ring. (5) RESOLVE THE MULTIPLIER CONFLICT: Show one combo multiplier (next to score) and one speed/boost multiplier (next to the speed bar), each explicitly labeled, eliminating the x4.0-vs-x1.0 ambiguity. (6) ALPINE IDENTITY: Introduce snow-white and ice-cyan into the world and lighting while reserving orange strictly for player action/boost/active states, giving a coherent cold-world / warm-action contrast. (7) POLISH: Animate the progress bar to match 7/18, add a subtle live pulse to the LIVE dot, and verify no HUD clipping at narrower widths. This preserves every required HUD element, restores the missing focal content, fixes the inverted hierarchy and data conflict, and converts a generic dashboard into a distinct, speed-driven alpine scene — all within offline HTML/CSS/SVG.
